title: "Go Preach My Gospel, (Saith the Lord,)
description: "Go Preach My Gospel, (Saith the Lord,) in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 128, headed “The Apostles' commission; or, The gospel attested by miracles, Mark 16. 15 &c. Matt. 28. 18 &c”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Go preach my gos-pel, (saith the Lord,) "Bid the whole earth my grace re-ceive; "He shall be sav'd that trusts my word, "He shall be damn'd that won't be-lieve.

lines: "Bid the whole earth my grace receive;
"He shall be sav'd that trusts my word,
"He shall be damn'd that won't believe.
"And ye shall prove my gospel true
"By all the works that I have done,
"By all the wonders ye shall do.
"Go heal the sick, go raise the dead,
"Go cast out devils in my name;
"I'm with you till the world shall end;
"All power is trusted to my hands,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
